# iroh 1.3.0, patched for Couch Co-App

This is iroh 1.3.0 as published on crates.io (https://github.com/n0-computer/iroh, commit 0072d7d84b233f9e7185eb676f049beaf557ac03; MIT OR Apache-2.0, whose texts are beside this file, taken from that commit since the crate ships only `LICENSE-BSD3`), with two changes, wired in by `[patch.crates-io]` in the workspace's `Cargo.toml`, marked "Couch Co-App" in the code:

- **A relay connection starts again when its entry in the relay map changes** (`src/socket.rs`'s `handle_relay_map_change`, `src/socket/transports.rs` and `src/socket/transports/relay.rs`'s `relay_map_change`, and `RelayActorMessage::RelayMapChange` with `RelayActor::restart_changed_relays` in `src/socket/transports/relay/actor.rs`). `Endpoint::insert_relay` and `remove_relay` now also stop each relay connection whose token differs from what the map holds for its relay now (a new token, or the relay removed), and the home relay's connection starts again at once. A connection to a relay outside the map without a token (another member's) is left alone. `ActiveRelayHandle` keeps the token each connection started with, and its own stop token.

**Why.** A relay connection reads its token from the map once, when it starts, so iroh 1.3 kept the old token until the connection had been idle for 60 s, and the home relay's for good. Couch Co-App registers relays while running (M26, ADR 0014), and found in M26a's first tests (`crates/couch-engine/tests/relay.rs`, mod `registered`, 2026-11-13) that, unpatched:
- a relay added after a dial to it was refused (the usual moment: a member is on a relay we lack, and its code is pasted) kept being dialed without its token;
- a new code for a relay refusing ours (rotated or revoked) never reached it while it was the home relay;
- a removed relay kept receiving its token.

Those three tests fail unpatched and pass with this change.

- **Relays for dialing only** (`src/net_report.rs`'s `DialOnlyRelays` and `add_report_history_and_set_preferred_relay`, `Builder::dial_only_relays` and `Endpoint::set_dial_only_relays` in `src/endpoint.rs`, `EndpointInner::set_dial_only_relays` in `src/socket.rs`). A set of the relay map's URLs, probed and dialed with their tokens like any other, but a candidate for the preferred (home) relay only when no other relay has a latency over the reports' last 5 minutes, counting only relays still in the map or heard in the report (one removed, or set aside for refusing us, answers nothing for us). So that the others are heard: QAD probes them first, and a full report isn't "enough" until one of them answered (still bounded by the probes' timeout). A report with no candidate leaves the home relay as it is unless it is no longer one (it became dial-only, left the map, or another relay answers again): then the best candidate over the last 5 minutes; the client remembers the home it gave apart from its last report, which a full report clears. Changing the set runs a full report (as a relay map change does). A limit: a relay that dies without leaving the map keeps counting as answering for up to 5 minutes (its latency stays in the reports' history), so falling back to a dial-only relay lags that long. `Endpoint::set_dial_only_relays` is called with both sets' relays while the map changes (`couch_net::endpoint::change_relays`).

**Why.** Our home relay is named in our signed record, which every room's members see. A relay a room passed on to us (M26b), or one lent for a join, has a code only that room's members can get, so iroh choosing it as home by speed left the members of our other rooms without a relay path to us. It must stay in the map, since a relay's token is looked up there when its connection starts. `crates/couch-engine/tests/relay.rs`, mod `dial_only`: `home_leaves_a_relay_that_becomes_dial_only_and_moves_back` fails without the rule (iroh picks by latency and order, both relays being as fast); `a_dial_only_relay_is_home_when_no_other_answers` holds either way and guards the fallback. `net_report::tests::dial_only_relays_are_home_only_when_no_other_answers` covers the choice itself, a full report's reset and a relay that left the map included (run it from a copy of this folder with an empty `[workspace]` table: it isn't a workspace member).

Everything else is unchanged.

To update: copy the new release over this folder (keeping `LICENSE-MIT` and `LICENSE-APACHE` if it still ships none), apply both changes again, and run `cargo test -p couch-engine --test relay`. A release that restarts relay connections on a map change and can keep a relay from becoming home needs no patch: then remove this folder, its line in `.gitignore` and the `[patch.crates-io]` line.
